_comment: The contract for a story-structure beat pack (story/canon/beats/) and for a beat map an agent writes against one (story/canon/MAPPING.md). story/tools/beat_map.py reads every rule from here. A pack is a rubric, not a formula: the map shows the author which beats a draft has, which it lacks, and which land early or late. DECODER SAFETY: comment keys at this TOP LEVEL ONLY.
_keysWhy: Keys starting with _ are comments and allowed anywhere in a pack. _commonNames (beat id → the names writers commonly use for it) is internal: it lets an agent recognise 'my all is lost moment' without that name appearing in anything the author is shown as ours.
_marksWhy: Titles of books whose names are marks. A pack's internal _lineage may say where a structure comes from; nothing an author is shown as ours (displayName, summary, bestFor, a beat's name, describe or lookFor) may use them.
_toleranceWhy: A beat counts as early or late only when it lands more than this fraction of the book outside its window. Windows are where the beat usually falls, as a fraction of the whole (0 = the first word, 1 = the last).
_middleWhy: The span the report calls 'the middle': where drafts most often go missing, so its missing beats are listed first.
_evidenceWhy: Every beat in a map quotes the chapter it is in, word for word (spacing, case and curly quotes aside). A quote that is not in that chapter is refused: it means the agent paraphrased or invented the beat, and the author would be told their draft has something it does not.
